GenerateMoveStateMachine (protected; add.rationale: Node-by-node against Tunneler.cs:69-85. Four MoveStates with identical ids (BITE_MOVE, BURROW_MOVE, BELOW_MOVE, DIZZY_MOVE), follow-ups bite->burrow, burrow->below, below->below (the terminal self-loop) and dizzy->bite on BOTH sides, same registration list order, same initial state (bite). No branch state on either side (EXECUTED, `monster_probes_b06.py branch-args`). Note that DIZZY_MOVE is an UNWIRED state in the game -- nothing assigns it as a FollowUpState and it is not the initial state, the same shape as monster_state_machine G2's Inklet INIT_RAND -- and the sim reaches it deliberately; that is the `get_stunned` entry below, not a graph divergence.

guards.what: The dig-out: C# routes it through CreatureCmd.Stun, the sim hand-splices the machine
guards.rationale: BurrowedPower.cs:24-36 runs, on the owner's block breaking: `tunneler.GetStunned()` (Tunneler.cs:128-132 -- IsStunned = true plus a TriggerAnim, NOTHING mechanical), then `CreatureCmd.Stun(base.Owner, tunneler.StillDizzyMove, "BITE_MOVE")`, then `PowerCmd.Remove<BurrowedPower>`. So the game's stunned turn is a SYNTHETIC `MoveState("STUNNED", StillDizzyMove, StunIntent())` with FollowUpStateId "BITE_MOVE" and MustPerformOnceBeforeTransitioning = true (seam steps 38-40); the machine's own DIZZY_MOVE is never entered. The sim instead has BurrowedPower call `owner.get_stunned()` (powers.py:2298-2304), and tunneler.py:44-48 does `machine.force_current_state(dizzy); self._current_move = dizzy` -- it reaches the unwired DIZZY_MOVE node and uses it as the stun. **Same observable, argued step by step rather than asserted.** (a) The turn performed: C# runs StillDizzyMove, whose whole body is `IsStunned = false` plus a WakeUp TriggerAnim (Tunneler.cs:134-138); the sim runs `_dizzy`, a `pass` (tunneler.py:62-63). Both are mechanically empty, so the turn is lost on both sides. (b) The intent shown: C#'s synthetic move carries StunIntent; DIZZY_MOVE carries StunIntent in C# too (Tunneler.cs:75) and Intent(MoveType.STUN) in the sim (tunneler.py:37). (c) The move after: C# transitions STUNNED -> "BITE_MOVE" at the next roll (deterministic, seam step 10); the sim's roll walks DIZZY_MOVE.follow_up -> BITE. (d) The state log: `ForceCurrentState` does not log on either side (seam step 34), and both then log BITE at the next roll -- and Tunneler has NO branch state, so no repeat rule or cooldown reads the log anyway, which is what makes the seam's G4 log-duplication observable inapplicable here. (e) The MustPerformOnceBeforeTransitioning pin C# sets and the sim does not: no roll happens between the splice and the performance, because the sim rolls only inside take_turn's telegraph (state_machine.py:320-330), so the pin has nothing to prevent. This unit therefore does NOT make seam G5 (next_move_key dropped for MachineMonsters) live: the sim never calls CreatureCmd.stun on a Tunneler at all -- the same self-emulation the seam already records for SlumberingBeetle, LagavulinMatriarch and TerrorEel. BurrowedPower's own two divergences (the AfterRemoved block dump, the block-break trigger) are audit/records/power/burrowed.json's gaps and are not re-verdicted here.

ONE MECHANISM ACROSS THIS BATCH (rule 3), recorded at every site: the sim's monster ports drop PowerCmd.Apply's `applier` argument. C# is `Apply<T>(choiceContext, target, amount, applier, cardSource)` (PowerCmd.cs:67) and passes `base.Creature` at Tunneler.cs:99 (BurrowedPower, applier=base.Creature); the sim's `PowerCmd.apply(hooks, target, power_cls, amount, applier=None)` (cmds.py:271-277) is called without it at tunneler.py:56. In C# a null applier additionally SKIPS the whole Hook.ModifyPowerAmountGiven pass (PowerCmd.cs:123-126) and changes the key FindExistingInstanceForStacking uses (PowerCmd.cs:78, :112). Same observable today, EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/monster_probes_b06.py applier`): the sim has exactly six listener definitions that can see the argument -- powers.py:1172/1181 (ViciousPower, gated `name != "vulnerable" or applier is not self.owner`, powers.py:1167), powers.py:3101/3106 (_PossessPower, gated `applier is self.owner and name == self._stat_id and target.side == "player" and delta < 0`, powers.py:3092-3099), relics/ruined_helmet.py:23-38 (gated on `target is self.player`, never on applier) and relics/unsettling_lamp.py:44-53 (gated `applier is not self.player`, unsettling_lamp.py:47). None can distinguish `None` from the applying monster for a power this unit applies. Named trigger: porting any listener that reads `applier` positively (a monster-applier-sensitive relic), or porting PowerInstanceType so stacking is keyed by applier.
